title: The Wise Little Girl
summary: A kind father and his clever child must answer three riddles for a powerful leader.
coverScene: A wise little girl stands before a king in a grand hall, holding a small fish.

sentences.text: Long ago, there lived two brothers who were poor farmers in a small village.
One brother had much wealth, but he was very mean and shared nothing with anyone.
The other brother had almost nothing, yet he was kind and always ready to help people.
Once, the poor brother gave a lovely horse to the rich king as a gift.
He wanted to show his respect because he was an honest man who valued peace.
The king was very pleased with the gift and asked the poor man how much land he owned.
The poor man explained that he was a simple farmer with very little property.
Hearing this, the king decided to give him a bag of gold coins.
When the rich brother learned about the gold, he became extremely angry and sad.
He felt that the king should have given the money to him instead.
The mean brother went quickly to the king and claimed that the horse was really his.
The king, who wanted to know the truth, gave them a difficult test.
He asked them three hard questions which must be solved before the next day.
If they failed, they would face serious trouble from the royal court.
The poor brother went home with a heavy heart, feeling completely alone and weak.
He had a smart little girl who always gave him good advice when problems appeared.
She listened carefully to the king questions and told her father not to worry.
The little girl knew exactly how each problem could be solved through smart thinking.
She believed that they would find a way to pass the test successfully.
The next morning, both brothers stood before the king to give their answers.
The rich brother spoke badly, but the poor brother provided the smart answers which his daughter had taught him.
The king was surprised and realized that the answers were too smart for the poor farmer.
When the king asked who had helped him, the honest man admitted that his little girl had solved the questions.
The king wanted to see this smart child and commanded that she be brought to the castle.
When the little girl arrived, the king gave her one final challenge to test her mind.
He told her to come to the castle neither dressed nor not dressed, neither walking nor riding.
The smart girl understood the king game and prepared a very special plan.
She wrapped herself in an old fishing net so that she was neither fully dressed nor not dressed.
Then she tied an animal to her feet and let the creature drag her along the road.
In this way, she was neither walking nor riding when she finally reached the royal gates.
The king was so amazed by her intelligence that he praised her greatly and let her father keep the gold.
The poor brother lived happily for many years with his wonderful family.
He always remembered how his smart daughter had saved them from big trouble.
People in the village talked about the smart child who solved the royal questions.
No one ever forgot the day when the poor farmer received the gold coins.
Life in the small village continued quietly while the family enjoyed their new wealth.
The king often thought about the wise little girl and her strange journey to the castle.
He knew that true intelligence could be found in the most surprising places.
Both brothers learned important lessons about life, love, and truth.
The rich brother finally understood that money could not buy everything.
He tried to change his ways and started to help his neighbors when they needed assistance.
The poor brother remained kind and always shared what little he had with others.
Their story became a famous tale which was told across the entire country for generations.
Children listened with wide eyes while their parents repeated the wonderful story.
Everybody agreed that the little girl was the smartest person in the whole country.
The king made sure that peace and quiet ruled over the land for all time.
And so the happy days went by without any further trouble for the honest farmer and his family.

sentences.text: In a secluded rural valley where time seemed suspended, two brothers toiled as humble farmers. Though bound by blood, their paths diverged sharply in spirit and fortune. The elder brother accumulated substantial wealth, yet his heart remained tightly shuttered against the needs of others. He hoarded his possessions, believing that charity was merely a foolish waste. Conversely, the younger brother possessed almost nothing of material value. Yet, his generous nature radiated warmth, and he was perpetually inclined to assist anyone in distress.

Driven by an innate sense of reverence and a desire for peace, the impoverished farmer decided to make a remarkable gesture. He selected his finest possession, a magnificent horse, and led it across the hills as a tribute to the sovereign. Not once did he anticipate a reward; rather, he simply wished to honor the monarch with integrity. Touched by such profound sincerity, the king received the magnificent animal with deep appreciation. He inquired gently about the farmer's livelihood, wanting to understand the circumstances of such a generous giver.

With quiet dignity, the farmer explained that his property consisted of little more than a patch of earth and a weathered cottage. Moved by the stark contrast between the man's poverty and his generous spirit, the king instructed his treasurer to bestow a heavy purse of gold upon him. It was a fortune that promised to transform the struggling farmer's daily existence. When news of this royal favor reached the ears of the elder brother, bitterness immediately poisoned his mind. He burned with jealousy, convinced that the monarch had committed a grave error by bypassing his own substantial estate.

Consumed by greed, the wealthy brother hurried to the royal palace to challenge the transaction. He boldly claimed that the magnificent horse had actually belonged to his own stables, accusing the younger sibling of theft and deception. Intrigued by the conflicting claims and determined to uncover the truth, the king devised a severe test. He commanded both men to solve three intricate riddles before the arrival of the following dawn. Failure to produce the correct answers, he warned, would result in harsh punishment from the royal court.

Returning to his modest dwelling, the poor farmer carried a burden heavier than any stone he had ever lifted. He felt entirely unequipped for the intellectual combat demanded by the throne. Fortunately, he shared his roof with a remarkably perceptive daughter whose mind was remarkably sharp. Having observed her father's distress, she listened carefully as he recounted the royal challenge. Noticing his despair, she urged him to cast aside his worries and trust in her guidance.

The clever girl possessed an intuitive grasp of human nature and logic, seeing straight through the riddles that had paralyzed her father. She assured him that they would outwit the king's tests through careful thought rather than brute force. Reassured by her steady confidence, the father regained a measure of hope as night fell over the valley. When morning arrived, the two brothers stood once again before the imposing gates of the royal palace. While the wealthy brother stumbled through clumsy and arrogant replies, the poor farmer recited the brilliant answers his daughter had carefully prepared.

Astonishment rippled through the royal court as the king listened to the precise and elegant solutions. It was immediately apparent that such sophisticated reasoning far exceeded the simple farmer's usual capabilities. Pressured by the monarch to reveal the true source of his wisdom, the honest man confessed the truth without hesitation. He explained that his young daughter had unraveled the difficult questions. Intrigued by this revelation, the king demanded that the extraordinary child be brought immediately to the castle for a final demonstration of her intellect.

Upon her arrival in the grand hall, the king decided to test the limits of her reputation with one final paradox. He commanded her to present herself before him neither dressed nor not dressed, and neither walking nor riding. A lesser mind would have faltered under the weight of such an impossible contradiction. However, the wise girl merely smiled, recognizing the playful nature of the royal challenge. She immediately set to work, determined to satisfy the monarch's exacting conditions with creative precision.

Returning briefly to the courtyard, she found an old, discarded fishing net and wrapped it securely around her frame. In this ingenious attire, she was neither fully clothed nor completely naked, satisfying the first half of the paradox. For the second requirement, she secured a strong hound to her ankles and permitted the creature to drag her slowly along the dirt road. Thus, she arrived at the royal gates neither walking on her own feet nor riding upon a mount. The king watched her approach from his balcony, utterly captivated by her brilliant solution.

Overwhelmed with admiration, the monarch praised the young girl publicly and confirmed that her father should retain every coin of the gold. The impoverished family returned to their village, where they lived comfortably for many years, shielded from sudden hardship. The father never forgot how his daughter's remarkable mind had rescued them from disaster. Meanwhile, the village buzzed with endless conversations about the clever child who had conquered the royal riddles. The king himself often pondered her ingenuity, realizing that true wisdom frequently resides in the most unexpected corners of society.

Gradually, the transformative experience softened the harsh edges of the wealthy brother's character. Witnessing the enduring happiness of his sibling, he finally comprehended that wealth alone could never purchase genuine respect or peace. He began to alter his conduct, offering assistance to struggling neighbors instead of turning them away. The kind brother continued his generous habits, sharing his newfound comfort with those in genuine need. Thus, the entire community settled into a quiet harmony, sustained by the lessons learned during that unforgettable test.

Generations later, villagers still gathered around hearths to recount the tale of the wise little girl. Children listened with wide eyes, absorbing the moral that intellect and kindness triumph over greed. The monarch ensured that peace prevailed throughout his domain, protecting his subjects from needless conflict. The memory of the humble farmer and his brilliant daughter endured as a symbol of hope. And so the peaceful days flowed onward, undisturbed by further trials for the grateful family.
